# Keyed archives and class resolution

`RSKeyedArchiver` records the logical state that each object writes through
`encodeWithCoder()`. `RSKeyedUnarchiver` first loads the archive for inspection.
On `$decode()`, it obtains current class generators, allocates instances with
`robjc_allocate()` without calling `initialize()`, and passes saved fields to
`initWithCoder()`. A singleton's allocation returns its shared instance.

The archive is an ordinary R list. Use `saveRDS()` and `readRDS()` for file
storage. The keyed format preserves repeated references to the same RObjC
object; plain R values form the boundary with R's serialization. Lists are
traversed for RObjC references.

## Built-in classes

Classes supplied by robjc are registered when the package loads. Their archive
records include a package name and stable class ID, so decoding needs no manual
mapping.

```{r}
library(robjc)

value <- RSString$new("hello")
archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$archive(list(value, value))
record <- archive$records[[1L]]
stopifnot(identical(record$package, "robjc"))
stopifnot(identical(record$class_id, "RSString"))

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(archive, path)
decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(readRDS(path))
stopifnot(nrow(decoder$showAllClasses()) == 0L)
classes <- decoder$showAllClasses(remove_default = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(classes$status, "automatic"))
restored <- decoder$decode()
unlink(path)
stopifnot(identical(restored[[1L]], restored[[2L]]))
stopifnot(identical(restored[[1L]]$value(), "hello"))
```

`showAllClasses()` omits automatically resolved classes by default. An empty
tibble means that no mapping needs attention. Use `remove_default = FALSE` to
inspect every class. `dictionaryWithAllClasses()` always returns all mappings.

## Classes in extension packages

Define the generator in the package namespace and register it from `.onLoad()`.
The `binding` argument is the namespace variable containing the generator.
The `id` is the stable identifier stored in archives: keep it when a binding,
displayed class name, or class version changes.

```{r eval=FALSE}
# R/Document.r in package "myrecords"
Document <- robjc::RSObjectClass(
  "Document", version = "1.0",
  public = list(
    title = NULL,
    initialize = function(title) {
      super$initialize()
      self$title <- title
      invisible(self)
    },
    encodeWithCoder = function(coder) {
      coder$encodeObjectForKey(self$title, "title")
    },
    initWithCoder = function(coder) {
      self$title <- coder$decodeObjectForKey("title")
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

# R/zzz.R in the same package
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  robjc::robjc_register_class(
    package = pkgname, id = "document", binding = "Document",
    generator = Document
  )
}
```

List `robjc` in the extension package's `Imports`. During decoding, the
unarchiver loads the recorded package if needed and obtains the current
generator from its registered namespace binding. The registry keeps names and
namespace identity, not the generator itself. Register protocol generators
with `robjc_register_protocol()` if they appear as archived values.

The stable ID and class version serve different purposes. `initWithCoder()` can
read `coder$savedClassVersion()` to handle an older field layout.

## Classes defined in a script

A generator outside a package namespace cannot use package registration.
`showAllClasses()` reports it as unresolved. Edit its `decoder_class` list
column, pass the tibble to `setClasses()`, then call `decode()`.
`showClass(class_key)` inspects one mapping. A dictionary offers the same
mapping interface with `RSString` keys and `RSNull$null` for unresolved values.

```{r}
Note <- RSObjectClass(
  "StrategyGuideNote", version = "1.0",
  public = list(
    title = NULL,
    initialize = function(title) {
      super$initialize()
      self$title <- title
      invisible(self)
    },
    encodeWithCoder = function(coder) coder$encodeObjectForKey(self$title, "title"),
    initWithCoder = function(coder) {
      self$title <- coder$decodeObjectForKey("title")
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$archive(Note$new("draft"))
decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(archive)
classes <- decoder$showAllClasses()
stopifnot(identical(classes$status, "unresolved"))
classes$decoder_class[1L] <- list(Note)
decoder$setClasses(classes)
stopifnot(identical(decoder$showClass(classes$class_key)$status, "manual"))
restored <- decoder$decode()
stopifnot(identical(restored$title, "draft"))
```

Each class explicitly records its fields under unique keys. A field can
contain an ordinary R value or another RObjC object. A list of RObjC objects
is traversed recursively, and repeated references remain shared. For a larger
object graph, see `vignette("robjc_encoding_use_case", package = "robjc")`.
The current archive format is `robjc-keyed-1`.
